explanations.explanation: That's it. Luke says the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem. The advance team went in and the village said no. That's a closed door, friend.

explanations.answer: They prepare a feast for Him
explanations.explanation: Not this time, friend. Luke 9:53 says the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem. The messengers came to make arrangements, and the village wanted no part of it. A feast would have been a very different story.

That's not what happens in this village, friend. The text says the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem. The messengers had gone in to make arrangements, and the answer was a plain no. Bringing the sick isn't in this scene.

Fire is right, friend. James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, ask, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?” That's a heavy question. They brought it straight to Jesus and asked Him.

Close on the weather, but no. James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, ask about calling down fire from heaven. The question is “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?” It's a serious moment, friend.

Not rain, friend. James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, ask, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?” They name fire, and the word consume goes with it. This is a heavy part of the passage.
True. Luke 9:55 says, “But Jesus turned and rebuked them.” That's all the verse tells us about how He answers. He turns, He rebukes, and then the story moves on.
It's actually true, friend. The text says, “But Jesus turned and rebuked them.” He doesn't say yes and He doesn't stay quiet. Luke gives us that one line and then moves on to the next village.
Not quite, friend. Luke 9:56 says, “And He and His disciples went on to another village.” They don't stay in that Samaritan village. They go on to another one.

False is right. Luke says, “And He and His disciples went on to another village.” They don't stay in the Samaritan village. They head on to the next one, and I bet there were a lot of questions on that walk.

explanations.answer: He has no place to lay His head
explanations.explanation: You've got it. Jesus says, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). Even a fox gets a den, and the One who made the foxes has no place to lay His head. The man said he'd follow wherever Jesus goes, and this is what that road looks like.

explanations.answer: He has a home waiting in Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: That's not what Jesus says, friend. Foxes have dens and birds have nests, “…but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” Jerusalem is where He's headed, but He says nothing here about a home waiting there. Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

explanations.answer: He has a house in every town
explanations.explanation: Nope, it's the other way around, friend. Jesus says, “…the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” Foxes get dens and birds get nests, but that's not how He describes Himself. The Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10), so that line is about Him.
Right on the mark. Jesus tells him, “You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.” That's the job He hands this man. Luke doesn't tell us what the man does next.
Jesus is headed for Jerusalem, so I see why you picked it. But He doesn't tell this man to wait there. What He says is, “You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.” Go is the word, not wait.

That sounds like a good plan, friend, but it's not in the text. Jesus tells him, “You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.” Nothing about rounding up a crowd. The task Jesus names is to proclaim the kingdom of God.

True. This man says, “I will follow You, Lord; but first let me bid farewell to my family.” He's the third person on the road with something to say to Jesus. And Jesus gives him an answer, which comes next in verse 62.
It's true, friend. The man says, “I will follow You, Lord; but first let me bid farewell to my family.” He starts with a yes and then adds a request. Jesus answers him, and that's the next verse.

Yes! Jesus says, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” The picture is a man with his hand on the plow who looks back. It's like trying to walk a straight line while staring over your shoulder, friend. You're not going where you're pointed.

That's a fair guess, because a plow is tiring just to think about. But Jesus never mentions resting. He says, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” The key is looking back.

Slow I can relate to, friend, because my first batch took all afternoon. But speed isn't what Jesus talks about here. He says, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” What matters in the picture is the man looking back.
